finding.claim: Unauthenticated /fetch2 fetches any http(s) URL supplied by the caller. The only check is a scheme check, so an attacker can reach loopback, internal services and cloud metadata (e.g. http://169.254.169.254/), and the first 200 bytes of the response come back in the JSON. Redirects are followed by default, which gives a second route to internal hosts.

trace.note: url taken from the query string
only checks urlparse(url).scheme in (http, https); no host or IP check
requests.get(url) issued, redirects followed, body[:200] returned to the caller

finding.guards_checked: is_http_url is a scheme allowlist only. No host/IP blocklist, no DNS resolution check, no redirect handling, and no auth on the route. Full read SSRF with response disclosure.

verdict.guard_found: none (is_http_url at validators.py:7 is a scheme-only check; no auth decorator or middleware on /fetch2; the stronger is_safe_url is used only on /fetch)
verdict.reason: views.py:19-22 takes the url from request.args, gates it only with the scheme-only is_http_url (validators.py:7), then calls requests.get(url, timeout=5) at line 22 with redirects followed by default and returns text[:200], so there is no host/IP guard and no auth.

finding.claim: /fetch validates the URL with is_safe_url, which resolves the hostname once with getaddrinfo. requests.get then resolves it a second time, so the resolved IP is not pinned. An attacker-controlled DNS name with a very short TTL can answer with a public IP for the check and 127.0.0.1 or 169.254.169.254 for the fetch (DNS rebinding / TOCTOU). Redirects are disabled, which closes the redirect route. The rebinding gap remains, and the 200-byte body is returned to the caller.

trace.note: url taken from the query string
first DNS resolution via socket.getaddrinfo; every returned IP is checked against private/loopback/link-local/reserved
requests.get(url) resolves the hostname again, with no pinning of the validated IP

finding.guards_checked: Scheme allowlist, hostname presence, and IP class checks (private, loopback, link-local, reserved) on all resolved addresses. allow_redirects=False is set. Missing: pinning the resolved IP to the connection, so the check and the fetch can see different addresses. getaddrinfo uses port 443 when none is given, which does not affect the IP check. Exploitation needs an attacker-run DNS server with a short TTL, so this is lower likelihood than finding 1.

verdict.guard_found: is_safe_url (validators.py:10-18) checks scheme and resolved IP classes once, with no IP pinning and no hostname allowlist; allow_redirects=False at views.py:14. These don't close the DNS rebinding gap.
verdict.reason: views.py:11-14 takes the url from the query string, validators.py:14 resolves it once for the IP check, and requests.get at views.py:14 resolves it again with no pinning, so a short-TTL rebinding DNS name can pass the check and then hit an internal IP.
